title: test-0092-GEN-INTEREST
passage: In the classroom, Mr. Sharma explained how loans work. 'When you borrow money, you pay back the principal plus interest,' he said. Rohan asked, 'So, if I borrow 10,000 for one year at 10% interest, I just pay back 1,000?' Mr. Sharma shook his head. 'No, Rohan. That 1,000 is only the interest; you must return the original 10,000 too. The total repayment is 11,000.' Priya then asked about EMIs. 'My brother says an EMI is just the total loan divided by the months.' Mr. Sharma corrected her, 'Not quite. An EMI includes both principal and interest, so it is always higher than that simple division.' He then discussed compounding. 'If interest is compounded half-yearly, you must halve the annual rate and double the number of time periods.' Rohan looked confused, 'But doesn't the interest rate increase every year with compounding?' Mr. Sharma smiled, 'No, the rate stays constant; it is the principal that grows as interest is added to it. Also, remember that for a six-month period, you must use T = 0.5 years in your calculations, not 6.' Finally, he warned, 'Always check for hidden fees, as a lower interest rate does not always mean the cheapest loan.'
